items.stem: Why is data quality critical to trustworthy AI outcomes?

options.text: Models learn patterns from data, so poor-quality data produces poor or biased predictions
options.rationale: Correct: 'garbage in, garbage out' - inaccurate or incomplete data degrades and can bias model outputs.

options.text: Data quality only affects report formatting
options.rationale: Data quality affects model behaviour, not just reports.

options.text: High-quality data removes the need for human oversight
options.rationale: Oversight remains necessary regardless of data quality.

options.text: AI ignores the training data entirely
options.rationale: Models depend directly on their training data.

items.explanation: Correct: 'garbage in, garbage out' - inaccurate or incomplete data degrades and can bias model outputs.

items.stem: A lead-scoring model consistently ranks one region lower because historical data under-represents it. This is an example of:

options.text: Bias arising from unrepresentative training data
options.rationale: Correct: skewed or unrepresentative data leads the model to encode and repeat that bias.
This is a data/fairness issue, not hardware.
Latency is unrelated to biased scoring.

options.text: Correct behaviour that needs no review
options.rationale: Biased outcomes require investigation and mitigation.

items.stem: Which TWO are principles of responsible/trusted AI?

options.text: Transparency about how AI makes decisions
options.rationale: Correct: transparency and explainability are core trusted-AI principles.
Correct: humans remain accountable and provide oversight of AI.

options.text: Maximising model size at any cost
options.rationale: Bigger is not a responsible-AI principle.

options.text: Hiding the use of AI from users
Ignoring data privacy to improve accuracy
options.rationale: Privacy must be respected; it is a core principle.

items.explanation: Correct: transparency and explainability are core trusted-AI principles.
